record.summary: Voluntary national guidelines from Malaysia's Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MOSTI) that set seven AI principles: fairness; reliability, safety and control; privacy and security; inclusiveness; transparency; accountability; and the pursuit of human benefit and happiness. Separate parts guide AI end users, policymakers, and developers, designers and technology providers. They call for testing, certification and risk and impact assessments, human oversight (human-in-the-loop, on-the-loop and in-command), consumer rights to an explanation, human contact and redress, and a feasibility study for an independent national AI advisory agency.
record.notes: Deputy Prime Minister Fadillah Yusof launched the guidelines on 20 Sep 2024; the MASTIC publication page dates them September 2024. They were developed as an action plan of the National AI Roadmap 2021-2025 (AI-RMAP), with input from the working committee of the National Blockchain and Artificial Intelligence Committee (NBAIC), Universiti Teknologi Malaysia, industry and civil society. The guidelines call themselves a living document to be reviewed and updated regularly and say they will be made available in Malay and English. The National AI Action Plan 2026-2030 cites them as published by MOSTI in 2023. AI Malaysia's voluntary AI Code of Ethics (AICE) puts their seven principles into practice.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. The guidelines PDF carries no date of its own; date_published is the launch date in MOSTI's press release. The National AI Action Plan's citation of a 2023 publication rests on that plan's text (MY-03), not on a file of this record. The summary's audiences, which version 1 took from background knowledge, are now confirmed by the guidelines and the press release.

status.quote: THE NATIONAL GUIDELINES ON AI GOVERNANCE & ETHICS Publication Date :- Sep 2024 Type :- MOSTI Related Policies

status.locator: How does AICE relate to the National Guidelines on AI Governance and Ethics (AIGE)?
status.quote: AICE provides practical guidance to help organisations operationalise the seven (7) AI Principles outlined in the National Guidelines on AI Governance and Ethics (AIGE)

legal_force.quote: As mentioned in the Preamble section, these national guidelines are on a voluntary for the stakeholders.

summary.quote: These are: • Fairness • Reliability, Safety and Control • Privacy and Security • Inclusiveness • Transparency • Accountability • Pursuit of human benefit and happiness

the three main stakeholders, namely (1) the society, consisting of users, workers, and consumers in general, (2) government agencies and policymakers, and (3) the industry, including developers and designers.
Developers and end-users are encouraged to carry out relevant testing and certification as well as risk and impact assessments to prevent any potential harm and mitigate risks.
Human oversight helps to ensure that AI systems do not undermine human autonomy through governance mechanisms such as human-in-the-loop (HITL), human-on-the-loop (HOTL), and human-in-command (HIC).

summary.locator: page 50, Part A, 2.3 Consumer protection principles in AI
summary.quote: The consumer must have the right to object and to be given explanation.

summary.locator: page 50, Part A, 2.3 Consumer protection principles in AI
summary.quote: Consumers must have the right to interact with a human instead of AI. Consumers must have the right to redress and compensation for any damages.

summary.locator: page 79, Part B, B4.0 The Independent Advisory Body
summary.quote: A feasibility study needs to be carried out to determine the requirements for the establishment of an independent national Advisory Agency.

notes.quote: two action plans have been initiated: the development of National Guidelines for AI Governance and Ethics and the Institutionalization of Responsible AI.

notes.locator: page 6, Foreword by the Deputy Prime Minister
notes.quote: the Working Committee of the National Blockchain and Artificial Intelligence Committee (NBAIC), academia, namely, Universiti Teknologi Malaysia
these National Guidelines will be reviewed regularly and updated to meet the requirements and expectations of stakeholders. The National Guidelines will be made available in both Malay and English.

judgment.status_reasoning: MOSTI launched the guidelines on 20 Sep 2024; the MASTIC page still lists them among MOSTI-related policies in Oct 2026, and AI Malaysia's AICE page of Oct 2026 treats their seven principles as the current reference. The guidelines call themselves a living document, but nothing stored shows a revised edition, replacement or withdrawal. 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands; legal force is non-binding because the guidelines say they are voluntary for stakeholders.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published 2024-09-20: MOSTI's press release reports the launch that day. The MASTIC page gives 'Sep 2024'; the guidelines PDF carries no date. The National AI Action Plan 2026-2030 cites the AIGE as published in 2023, which no file of this record supports.
